_instructions: Score every hint for the pair it sits under. 'already_served' is context only: do not score it.

hints.explanation: A saucer sits under a teacup, and aliens fly flying saucers in sci-fi.

lines.ALIEN: In science fiction, aliens arrive in flying saucers.
lines.CUP: A saucer is the small plate under a cup.

hints.explanation: In Greek myth, Sirens lured sailors with their song, and ambulances race by with wailing sirens.

lines.AMBULANCE: Ambulances use loud sirens to clear the road.
lines.SONG: In Greek myth, the Sirens' song lured sailors toward the rocks.

hints.explanation: An ant colony is usually led by an egg-laying queen, and the queen is the strongest chess piece.

lines.ANT: A typical ant colony has one or more queens that lay the eggs.
lines.CHESS: The queen is the most powerful piece in chess.

hints.explanation: Bobbing for apples is a traditional Halloween party game.

lines.APPLE: In apple bobbing, you try to grab floating apples with your teeth.
lines.HALLOWEEN: Bobbing for apples is a classic Halloween party game.

hints.explanation: A shirt sleeve covers the arm, and a tattoo covering most of an arm is called a sleeve.

lines.ARM: A sleeve is the part of a garment that covers the arm.
lines.TATTOO: A sleeve tattoo covers much or all of an arm.

hints.explanation: Apollo is a Greek god, and NASA's Apollo program landed astronauts on the Moon.

lines.ASTRONAUT: NASA's Apollo missions carried astronauts to the Moon.
lines.GOD: Apollo is the Greek god of music, light and prophecy.

hints.explanation: Buzz Aldrin is an Apollo 11 astronaut, and Buzz Lightyear is the space-ranger toy in Toy Story.

lines.ASTRONAUT: Buzz Aldrin walked on the Moon on Apollo 11.
lines.TOY: Buzz Lightyear is the space-ranger action figure in Toy Story.

hints.explanation: To monitor is to watch closely, and parents use a baby monitor to keep an ear or eye on a sleeping baby.

lines.BABY: A baby monitor lets parents hear or see a baby from another room.
lines.WATCH: To monitor something is to watch it closely over time.

hints.explanation: Mary Poppins flies in with her umbrella and carries a seemingly bottomless carpet bag.

lines.BAG: Mary Poppins pulls a lamp and more out of her carpet bag.
lines.UMBRELLA: Mary Poppins floats down from the sky holding her umbrella.

hints.explanation: Coach is a famous handbag brand, and sports coaches blow whistles.

lines.BAG: Coach is a well-known handbag and leather goods brand.
lines.WHISTLE: A sports coach often carries a whistle.

hints.explanation: A masquerade is a ball where the guests wear masks.

lines.BALL: A masquerade ball is a formal dance party in costume.
lines.MASK: Guests at a masquerade hide their faces behind masks.

hints.explanation: A classic knock-knock joke ends "Orange you glad I didn't say banana?"

lines.BANANA: In the joke, "Banana who?" repeats until the punchline.

hints.explanation: In the limbo, dancers lean back to pass under a bar that gets lower each round.

lines.BAR: Limbo dancers try to pass under a horizontal bar without touching it.
lines.DANCE: The limbo is a dance contest that began in Trinidad and Tobago.

hints.explanation: Peppermint bark, chocolate topped with crushed peppermint candy, is a popular Christmas treat.

lines.BARK: Peppermint bark is a candy of chocolate layers topped with crushed peppermint pieces.
lines.CHRISTMAS: Peppermint flavors, like candy canes, are a classic part of Christmas sweets.

hints.explanation: A baserunner slides into a base hoping to be called safe.

lines.BASE: Runners often slide into a base.
lines.SAFE: A good slide can beat the tag so the umpire calls the runner safe.

hints.explanation: A bat is both the club swung in baseball and a classic Halloween creature.

lines.BASEBALL: Batters swing a bat at the pitch in baseball.
lines.HALLOWEEN: Bats are a staple of Halloween decorations, alongside ghosts and witches.

hints.explanation: You strike a match to light it, and in baseball a strike is a missed swing or a called pitch in the zone.

lines.BASEBALL: In baseball, three strikes and the batter is out.
lines.MATCH: You strike a match against the box to light it.

hints.explanation: In the classic snake-charmer scene, a cobra rises out of a basket.

lines.BASKET: The snake charmer's cobra famously rises from a wicker basket.
lines.CHARM: Snake charmers traditionally perform with cobras, swaying to a pipe.

hints.explanation: Basketball is played on a court, and shopping malls have food courts.

lines.BASKETBALL: Basketball is played on a rectangular court with a hoop at each end.
lines.FOOD: A food court is an area of a mall or airport with many food counters and shared seating.

hints.explanation: Judges wear black robes in court, and a bathrobe is worn after a bath.

lines.BATH: A bathrobe is worn after a bath or shower.
lines.JUDGE: Judges traditionally wear black robes on the bench.

hints.explanation: A loofah bath sponge is the dried fiber of a gourd that can also be eaten as a vegetable when young.

lines.BATH: Loofah sponges are used to scrub skin in the bath or shower.
lines.VEGETABLE: Young loofah gourds are cooked as a vegetable in parts of Asia.

hints.explanation: Yogi Bear lives in Jellystone Park.

lines.BEAR: Yogi Bear is the picnic-basket-stealing cartoon bear.
lines.JELLY: Yogi Bear's home is Jellystone Park, a play on Yellowstone.

hints.explanation: In boxing, a heavyweight champion holds a famous title belt.

lines.BELT: Boxing champions, heavyweights included, are awarded championship belts.
lines.BOXING: Heavyweight is the heaviest weight class in professional boxing.

hints.explanation: George Washington was the first U.S. president, and his portrait is on the one-dollar bill.

lines.BILL: George Washington's portrait appears on the U.S. one-dollar bill.
lines.FIRST: George Washington was the first president of the United States.

hints.explanation: Captain Jack Sparrow is the pirate of Pirates of the Caribbean, and a sparrow is a small songbird.

lines.BIRD: A sparrow is a small, common songbird.
lines.JACK: Johnny Depp plays Captain Jack Sparrow in the Pirates of the Caribbean films.

hints.explanation: Woodstock is Snoopy's little yellow bird friend, and the 1969 Woodstock festival was billed as three days of peace and music.

lines.BIRD: Woodstock is the small yellow bird in Peanuts.
lines.PEACE: The 1969 Woodstock festival was promoted as "3 Days of Peace & Music."

hints.explanation: Black Friday is the big shopping day right after U.S. Thanksgiving.

lines.BLACK: Black Friday is known for big holiday sales.
lines.THANKSGIVING: Black Friday falls the day after U.S. Thanksgiving.

hints.explanation: In volleyball, attackers spike the ball and defenders leap at the net to block it.

lines.BLOCK: In volleyball, players jump at the net to block an opponent's attack.
lines.SPIKE: A spike is a hard downward hit in volleyball.

hints.explanation: A plank is a long flat board, and the plank is also a classic core exercise.

lines.BOARD: A plank is a long, flat piece of wood, essentially a board.
lines.GYM: The plank, holding your body straight on your forearms, is a familiar gym exercise.

hints.explanation: Battleship is a classic board game in which players try to sink each other's ships.

lines.BOARD: Battleship is a classic two-player board game.
lines.SINK: In Battleship, you call out shots to sink your opponent's hidden fleet.

hints.explanation: Row, Row, Row Your Boat is the classic song sung as a round.

lines.BOAT: The song tells you to row your boat gently down the stream.
lines.ROUND: A round is a song where voices start at different times, and Row, Row, Row Your Boat is a favorite one.

hints.explanation: Stunt doubles and body doubles stand in for actors in films.

lines.BODY: A body double stands in for an actor in certain shots.
lines.STUNT: A stunt double performs an actor's risky stunts.

hints.explanation: Pulling a turkey's wishbone, often after Thanksgiving dinner, is a tradition for making a wish.

lines.BONE: The wishbone is a forked bone from a bird's breast, such as a turkey's.
lines.WISH: Two people pull a turkey's wishbone, and the one with the bigger piece makes a wish.

hints.explanation: In Super Mario games, Bowser is the boss Mario must beat to rescue Princess Peach.

lines.BOSS: Bowser is the final boss in many Super Mario games.
lines.PRINCESS: Bowser often kidnaps Princess Peach in the Mario series.

hints.explanation: A bottle opener pops off caps, and a season opener is a team's first game of the year.

lines.BOTTLE: A bottle opener removes bottle caps.
lines.SEASON: A season opener is the first game of a sports season (or first episode of a TV season).

hints.explanation: Minnie Mouse is known for the big polka-dot bow on her head.

lines.BOW: Minnie Mouse's signature look includes a large bow, usually red with white polka dots.
lines.MOUSE: Minnie Mouse is Mickey Mouse's girlfriend in Disney cartoons.

hints.explanation: A curtsy is the bent-knee greeting traditionally made to a queen, the counterpart of a bow.

lines.BOW: A curtsy is the traditional counterpart of a bow, made by bending the knees.
lines.QUEEN: Curtsying is a traditional way to greet a queen.

hints.explanation: In Doctor Who, the Doctor travels through time in the TARDIS, which looks like an old blue police box.

lines.BOX: The TARDIS is disguised as a blue British police box.
lines.DOCTOR: The TARDIS is the time machine of the Doctor in the long-running series Doctor Who.

hints.explanation: In Greek myth Pandora opened a forbidden box of troubles, and Pandora is also a music streaming service.

lines.BOX: In the popular telling of the myth, Pandora opened a box that released the world's troubles.
lines.MUSIC: Pandora is a music streaming service known for its personalized radio stations.

hints.explanation: Einstein's name is shorthand for genius, and his brain was preserved and studied after his death.

lines.BRAIN: After Einstein died in 1955, his brain was removed and studied by scientists.
lines.GENIUS: Calling someone an Einstein means calling them a genius.

hints.explanation: Snoopy is Charlie Brown's dog in the Peanuts comic strip.

lines.BROWN: Snoopy belongs to Charlie Brown in Peanuts.
lines.DOG: Snoopy is a beagle, and one of the most famous cartoon dogs.

hints.explanation: To scrub is to clean hard with a brush, and scrub is also land covered in low, stunted bushes.

lines.BRUSH: A scrub brush is a stiff brush for scrubbing floors and pots.
lines.BUSH: Scrub is a type of landscape covered with low bushes and small trees.

hints.explanation: Bubble wrap cushions packages, and gift wrap covers presents.

lines.BUBBLE: Bubble wrap is plastic sheeting filled with poppable air bubbles.
lines.GIFT: Gift wrap is the paper used to wrap presents.

hints.explanation: The scarab is a dung beetle that ancient Egyptians treated as a sacred symbol.

lines.BUG: A scarab is a kind of beetle, a bug that rolls balls of dung.
lines.EGYPT: Scarab amulets and carvings were common in ancient Egypt, linked to the sun god Khepri.

hints.explanation: Computers suffer from bugs, which are coding errors, and from viruses, which are malicious programs.

lines.BUG: A computer bug is an error in a program.
lines.VIRUS: A computer virus is a malicious program that spreads between machines.

hints.explanation: LEGO pieces are called bricks, and many buildings are made of brick.

lines.BUILDING: Many buildings are built from fired clay bricks.
lines.LEGO: The classic LEGO piece is known as a LEGO brick.

hints.explanation: A tall building has many stories, and a tall story is an exaggerated tale.

lines.STORY: A tall story (or tall tale) is a wildly exaggerated story.

hints.explanation: London is famous for its red double-decker buses.

lines.BUS: A double-decker is a bus with two levels of seats.
lines.LONDON: Red double-decker buses are an icon of London.

hints.explanation: Ms. Frizzle drives the Magic School Bus.

lines.BUS: Ms. Frizzle's class rides a school bus that can shrink, fly and dive.
lines.MAGIC: The Magic School Bus is led by teacher Ms. Frizzle (a classic kids' series).

hints.explanation: Cabbage Patch Kids are famous dolls whose backstory says they came from a cabbage patch.

lines.CABBAGE: A cabbage patch is a garden plot of cabbages.
lines.KID: Cabbage Patch Kids are a famous doll line from the 1980s.

hints.explanation: The rib cage protects the heart and lungs.

lines.CAGE: The rib cage is the bony cage around your chest.

hints.explanation: To leap is to jump, and a leap year adds February 29 to the calendar.

lines.CALENDAR: A leap year adds an extra day to the calendar, roughly every four years.
lines.JUMP: A leap is a big jump.

hints.explanation: Venice, Italy, is famous for its canals and gondolas.

lines.CANAL: Venice is built around canals, with the Grand Canal at its heart.
lines.ITALY: Venice is one of Italy's most famous cities.

hints.explanation: A candy cane is a striped Christmas candy, and a cane is a walking stick.

lines.CANDY: Candy canes are striped, hook-shaped peppermint candies.
lines.STICK: A cane is a walking stick.

hints.explanation: Old cannons were fired by lighting a fuse, and a stick of dynamite is set off the same way.

lines.CANNON: Many old cannons were fired by lighting a fuse at the touch hole.
lines.DYNAMITE: A stick of dynamite is classically lit with a fuse.

hints.explanation: Tchaikovsky's 1812 Overture calls for real cannon fire in its finale.

lines.CANNON: The score of Tchaikovsky's 1812 Overture includes cannon shots, often fired at U.S. Fourth of July concerts.
lines.MUSIC: Tchaikovsky was a Russian composer of famous music like Swan Lake and The Nutcracker.

hints.explanation: Cap'n Crunch, a cartoon sea captain, is the mascot of a famous cereal.

lines.CAPTAIN: Cap'n Crunch is a cartoon captain in a naval hat.
lines.CEREAL: Cap'n Crunch is a sweet corn-and-oat breakfast cereal.

hints.explanation: In Moby-Dick, Captain Ahab obsessively hunts the white whale.

lines.CAPTAIN: Captain Ahab commands the ship Pequod in Moby-Dick.
lines.WHALE: Ahab hunts Moby Dick, a great white whale.

hints.explanation: A car can have a manual transmission, which is what "driving stick" means, and comes with an owner's manual.

lines.CAR: A car's owner's manual explains its features, and some cars have manual gearboxes.
lines.STICK: Driving stick means driving a car with a manual transmission.

hints.explanation: You drive a car, and a thumb drive is a pocket USB storage stick.

lines.THUMB: A thumb drive is a small USB flash drive about the size of a thumb.

hints.explanation: Cards come in suits like hearts and spades, and your strong suit is what you do best.

lines.CARD: A deck of cards has four suits.
lines.STRONG: Your strong suit is the thing you are best at.

hints.explanation: Aladdin flies on a magic carpet.

lines.CARPET: Aladdin rides a magic carpet in the Disney film.
lines.FLY: Aladdin and Jasmine fly over the city on the carpet.

hints.explanation: A lawyer argues court cases and files lawsuits.

lines.CASE: Lawyers take on and argue legal cases.
lines.SUIT: Lawyers handle lawsuits, and many wear business suits to court.

hints.explanation: A cat is said to have nine lives, and someone blissfully happy is on cloud nine.

lines.CAT: In the old saying, a cat has nine lives.
lines.CLOUD: Being on cloud nine means being extremely happy.

hints.explanation: Champagne is served in a tall glass called a flute, and the flute is a woodwind instrument.

lines.CHAMPAGNE: A champagne flute is a tall, narrow glass.
lines.INSTRUMENT: The flute is a woodwind instrument played by blowing across a hole.

hints.explanation: A leopard can't change its spots, says the proverb about people who never really change.

lines.CHANGE: The proverb a leopard can't change its spots means a person's nature doesn't change.
lines.SPOT: Leopards are covered in dark spots called rosettes.

hints.explanation: Cinderella's prince is widely known as Prince Charming.

lines.CHARM: The storybook hero Prince Charming is named for his charm.
lines.CINDERELLA: Cinderella marries a prince, often called Prince Charming.

hints.explanation: To lure is to charm or tempt, and a lure is an artificial fishing bait.

lines.CHARM: To lure someone is to charm or tempt them in.
lines.FISHING: A fishing lure is an artificial bait that attracts fish.

hints.explanation: Swiss cheese is known for its holes, and the Swiss Army knife is a famous multi-tool.

lines.CHEESE: Swiss cheese is known for its holes.
lines.TOOL: The Swiss Army knife is a pocket multi-tool.

hints.explanation: In Pixar's Ratatouille a rat becomes a chef in Paris, and ratatouille is a French vegetable stew.

lines.CHEF: In Ratatouille, Remy the rat cooks as a chef in a Paris restaurant.
lines.FRANCE: Ratatouille is a vegetable stew from southern France, and the film is set in Paris.

hints.explanation: Chicks peck at their food, and a pecking order is a ranking named for how hens settle who is boss by pecking.

lines.CHICK: Chicks peck at the ground for seeds and grit.
lines.ORDER: A pecking order is a ranking of status, named for how chickens establish rank by pecking.

hints.explanation: Wild giant pandas live only in China, and China lends pandas to zoos around the world.

lines.CHINA: In the wild, giant pandas are found only in the mountains of China.
lines.ZOO: Giant pandas are star attractions at the zoos that host them, usually on loan from China.

hints.explanation: A nun is a woman in a religious order of the church, and nuns are addressed as Sister.

lines.CHURCH: Nuns are women who serve in a religious order of the church.
lines.SISTER: Nuns are traditionally called Sister, as in Sister Mary.

hints.explanation: The pope leads the Catholic Church, and white smoke from the Sistine Chapel signals that a new pope has been chosen.

lines.CHURCH: The pope is the leader of the Roman Catholic Church.
lines.SMOKE: During a papal election, white smoke from the Sistine Chapel chimney means a new pope has been elected.

hints.explanation: The prince finds Cinderella when the glass slipper fits her foot.

lines.CINDERELLA: Cinderella leaves behind a glass slipper at the ball.
lines.FOOT: The prince tries the slipper on each maiden's foot until it fits Cinderella.

hints.explanation: Crop circles are patterns flattened into fields of crops, and farms grow crops.

lines.CIRCLE: Crop circles are large patterns flattened into fields of grain.
lines.FARM: Farms grow crops such as wheat and corn.

hints.explanation: The Arctic Circle is a line of latitude that rings the far north of the globe.

lines.CIRCLE: The Arctic Circle is an imaginary circle of latitude around the Arctic.
lines.NORTH: The Arctic is the region around the North Pole, at the top of the world.

hints.explanation: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals on display, like an early zoo or a traveling circus show.

lines.CIRCUS: Traveling circuses once toured with menageries of exotic animals.
lines.ZOO: Royal and traveling menageries of exotic animals were forerunners of the modern zoo.

hints.explanation: Tide is a detergent for getting laundry clean, and the Moon's gravity drives the ocean tides.

lines.CLEAN: Tide is a laundry detergent brand sold for washing clothes clean.
lines.MOON: The Moon's gravity is the main driver of Earth's ocean tides.

hints.explanation: A court jester was a clown-like entertainer in a royal court.

lines.CLOWN: A jester played the fool, much like a clown.
lines.COURT: Jesters entertained kings and queens at court.

hints.explanation: A blazer is a tailored jacket close kin to the sport coat, and the Portland Trail Blazers are an NBA team.

lines.COAT: A blazer is a tailored jacket, a type of coat.
lines.SPORT: A blazer is much like a sport coat, and the Trail Blazers play pro basketball.

hints.explanation: A ZIP code is the five-digit postal code used to sort U.S. mail.

lines.CODE: A ZIP code is a postal code (ZIP stands for Zone Improvement Plan).
lines.MAIL: U.S. mail is addressed and sorted using ZIP codes.

hints.explanation: A classic glass prism has triangle-shaped ends and splits white light into a rainbow of colors.

lines.COLOR: A prism spreads white light out into its separate colors.
lines.TRIANGLE: The classic glass prism is a triangular prism, with a triangle at each end.

hints.explanation: Fine print is the small type in a contract, and fine itself can mean very thin or small.

lines.CONTRACT: Reading the fine print means checking every detail of a contract.
lines.SMALL: Fine print is the small type where the details are tucked away, and fine grains are very small ones.

hints.explanation: A country club is a private social club, often built around a golf course, and golfers swing clubs.

lines.COUNTRY: A country club is a private club, often with a golf course, pool and dining room.
lines.GOLF: Golfers hit the ball with clubs, such as drivers, irons and putters.

hints.explanation: In Jack and the Beanstalk, Jack trades the family cow for a handful of magic beans.

lines.COW: In the fairy tale, Jack's mother is furious that he swapped their cow for beans.
lines.JACK: Jack's magic beans grow into the giant beanstalk he climbs.

hints.explanation: Cowboys wear spurs strapped at the heel of their boots.

lines.COWBOY: Spurs are a classic part of a cowboy's gear.
lines.HEEL: Spurs attach at the heel of a riding boot.

hints.explanation: The Wall Street Crash of 1929 is history's most famous stock market crash.

lines.CRASH: The stock market crash of 1929 is known as the Wall Street Crash.
lines.STREET: Wall Street is the famous financial street in New York City.

hints.explanation: In Peter Pan, the crocodile swallowed a clock, so its tick-tock warns Captain Hook it is near, and watches tick-tock too.

lines.CROCODILE: In Peter Pan, the crocodile that swallowed a clock is known for its tick-tock sound.
lines.WATCH: A mechanical watch makes a ticking sound.

hints.explanation: Eating crow and eating humble pie both mean being forced to admit you were wrong.

lines.CROW: To eat crow is to humbly admit a mistake.
lines.PIE: To eat humble pie is to apologize and accept humiliation.

hints.explanation: Edgar Allan Poe's The Raven is a famous poem, and ravens are close cousins of crows.

lines.CROW: Ravens and crows belong to the same bird genus, Corvus.
lines.POETRY: The Raven, by Edgar Allan Poe, is one of the best-known American poems.

hints.explanation: A crown is worn on the head, and a popular saying goes "heavy is the head that wears the crown."

lines.CROWN: A crown sits on the head, and the top of the head is also called the crown.
lines.HEAVY: "Heavy is the head that wears the crown" adapts Shakespeare's "Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown."

hints.explanation: Mints freshen your mouth, and a mint is where coins are made.

lines.CURRENCY: A mint is the facility that makes coin currency.

hints.explanation: You shuffle a deck of cards, and the shuffle is also a dance step.

lines.DANCE: The shuffle is a dance step with sliding, scuffing feet.
lines.DECK: You shuffle a deck of cards to mix them up.

hints.explanation: A prom is a formal school dance, and picking a prom dress is a big part of the night.

lines.DANCE: A prom is a formal dance held by many U.S. high schools.
lines.DRESS: Many prom-goers shop for a special prom dress.

hints.explanation: A conga line is a party dance where people follow each other in a long line.

lines.DANCE: The conga is a dance with Cuban roots, done in a long chain at parties.
lines.LINE: Dancers in a conga line hold the person in front and snake around the room.

hints.explanation: A blind date is set up between two strangers, and blinds cover a window.

lines.DATE: A blind date is a date between people who have never met.
lines.WINDOW: Window blinds are slatted shades that cover a window.

hints.explanation: Martin Luther King Jr. gave the I Have a Dream speech and is honored each January on MLK Day.

lines.DAY: MLK Day is a U.S. federal holiday held on the third Monday of January.
lines.DREAM: MLK delivered his I Have a Dream speech at the 1963 March on Washington.

hints.explanation: Labor means work, and Labor Day honors American workers each September.

lines.DAY: Labor Day is a U.S. holiday on the first Monday of September.
lines.WORK: Labor is another word for work.

hints.explanation: A phone dies when its battery runs out, and a fully drained battery is called dead.

lines.DEAD: An empty battery is called a dead battery.

hints.explanation: The Dead Sea is so salty that swimmers float easily on it.

lines.DEAD: The Dead Sea is named for being too salty for fish to live in.
lines.SEA: The Dead Sea is one of the saltiest bodies of water on Earth.

hints.explanation: To flambe a dish is to pour on liquor and set it alight, a showy finish for desserts like bananas Foster.

lines.DESSERT: Bananas Foster and cherries jubilee are classic flambe desserts.
lines.FLAME: To flambe is to light liquor on food so it briefly bursts into flame.

hints.explanation: Tide is a laundry detergent brand, and to turn the tide is to reverse the course of events.

lines.DETERGENT: Tide is a well-known laundry detergent.
lines.TURN: To turn the tide means to reverse how things are going.

hints.explanation: An angry mob in stories carries torches and pitchforks, and the devil is often drawn holding a pitchfork.

lines.DEVIL: Cartoon devils are often drawn holding a pitchfork.
lines.TORCH: Torches and pitchforks is the classic image of an angry village mob in old monster movies.

hints.explanation: A meteor shower streaks across the night sky, and a giant space-rock impact is linked to the dinosaurs' extinction.

lines.DINOSAUR: Scientists link the end of the non-bird dinosaurs to a huge asteroid impact, often pictured as a giant meteor.
lines.SHOWER: A meteor shower is a night of many shooting stars.

hints.explanation: In slang, to "dish" and to "spill the tea" both mean to share gossip.

lines.DISH: To dish (or dish the dirt) is slang for sharing gossip.
lines.TEA: "Spill the tea" is slang for sharing gossip.

hints.explanation: A Lab is a Labrador retriever, and a lab is where science experiments happen.

lines.DOG: Labrador retrievers, called Labs, are a popular dog breed.
lines.SCIENCE: Scientists run experiments in a lab (short for laboratory).

hints.explanation: The Saint Bernard is a big rescue dog breed, and Valentine's Day is named for Saint Valentine.

lines.DOG: The Saint Bernard is a giant dog breed famous for Alpine rescues.
lines.VALENTINE: Valentine's Day is named after Saint Valentine.

hints.explanation: Porcelain is also called china, and a china doll is a porcelain doll.

lines.DOLL: A china doll is a doll made of glazed porcelain.
lines.PORCELAIN: Porcelain dishes are often simply called china.

hints.explanation: In cartoon gags, a heavy anvil drops onto an unlucky character.

lines.DROP: Cartoons such as Looney Tunes often drop an anvil on a character's head.
lines.HEAVY: An anvil is a heavy iron block that blacksmiths hammer metal on.

hints.explanation: A cough drop is a lozenge that soothes a sore throat.

lines.DROP: A cough drop is a medicated candy lozenge.
lines.THROAT: Cough drops are sucked to soothe an irritated throat.

hints.explanation: Garden gnomes are lawn ornaments of little bearded folk much like the dwarfs of fairy tales.

lines.DWARF: Gnomes and dwarfs are both small, bearded figures from European folklore.
lines.GARDEN: Garden gnomes are popular ornaments for gardens and lawns.

hints.explanation: The fierce screech movies use for a bald eagle is often really a red-tailed hawk's call.

lines.EAGLE: Bald eagles have fairly weak, chirpy calls, so films often dub in a hawk's screech.
lines.HAWK: The red-tailed hawk's raspy screech is the classic bird-of-prey cry heard in movies.

hints.explanation: "Hotel California" is a famous song by the Eagles.

lines.EAGLE: The rock band Eagles recorded "Hotel California" (1976).
lines.HOTEL: "Hotel California" sings of a mysterious hotel.

hints.explanation: Bungee jumpers leap from great heights tied to a stretchy elastic cord.

lines.ELASTIC: A bungee cord is a strong elastic rope that stretches and springs back.
lines.JUMP: A bungee jump is a leap from a bridge or platform while attached to a bungee cord.

hints.explanation: A circuit breaker trips to cut off electricity during an overload.

lines.ELECTRICITY: A circuit breaker shuts off electricity to protect a circuit.
lines.TRIP: An overloaded circuit breaker is said to trip.

hints.explanation: Shakespeare wrote the comedy All's Well That Ends Well.

lines.END: All's Well That Ends Well is a Shakespeare play title.
lines.WELL: The title promises that all is well if it ends well.

hints.explanation: Helen of Troy is the face that launched a thousand ships, the beauty the Greeks sailed to Troy to win back.

lines.FACE: Christopher Marlowe called Helen of Troy the face that launched a thousand ships.
lines.SHIP: In Greek myth, a huge fleet of Greek ships sailed to Troy to bring Helen back.

hints.explanation: The Munsters is a classic sitcom about a friendly family of monsters, led by a Frankenstein-style dad.

lines.FAMILY: The Munsters follows the everyday life of the Munster family.
lines.MONSTER: Herman Munster is modeled on Frankenstein's monster, and his wife Lily is a vampire.

hints.explanation: The Incredibles is Pixar's film about the Parr family, who are all superheroes.

lines.FAMILY: The Incredibles follows the Parr family, parents and kids together.
lines.SUPERHERO: Each member of the Parr family in The Incredibles has a superhero power.

hints.explanation: A fan spins on blades, and Blade is Marvel's famous vampire hunter.

lines.FAN: A ceiling fan turns on spinning blades.
lines.VAMPIRE: Blade is a Marvel vampire hunter, played by Wesley Snipes in the films.

hints.explanation: Hermes is the Greek messenger god, and Hermès is a French luxury fashion house.

lines.FASHION: Hermès is a famous French luxury fashion brand.
lines.GOD: Hermes is the Greek messenger god with winged sandals.

hints.explanation: Fireworks throw sparks, and a magical kiss is said to make sparks fly.

lines.FIREWORKS: Fireworks shower glowing sparks across the sky.
lines.KISS: "Sparks flying" describes the thrill of a romantic kiss.

hints.explanation: A piranha is a sharp-toothed fish, and Piranha Plants are biting plants in Super Mario games.

lines.FISH: Piranhas are South American freshwater fish with sharp teeth.
lines.PLANT: Piranha Plants pop out of pipes to bite Mario.

hints.explanation: In legend, the phoenix bursts into flame and is reborn from its own ashes.

lines.FLAME: Flames leave ashes behind when something burns.
lines.PHOENIX: In legend, a phoenix rises again from its own ashes.

hints.explanation: Flames burn, and a comedy roast is a string of burns, or witty insults.

lines.FLAME: Flames burn, and to flame someone online means to insult them harshly.
lines.ROAST: A comedy roast is a show of burns aimed at a guest of honor.

hints.explanation: The fly on a pair of pants often closes with a zipper.

lines.FLY: A fly is the opening at the front of pants, often closed by a zipper.
lines.PANTS: Many pants zip up with a zipper.

hints.explanation: Hunger makes you want food, and The Hunger Games is the famous book and film series.

lines.FOOD: Hunger is the feeling of needing food.
lines.GAME: The Hunger Games is a book and film series about a televised survival contest.

hints.explanation: Bigfoot is a legendary ape-like creature, and in the 1988 film Big, Tom Hanks plays a giant floor piano with his feet.

lines.FOOT: Bigfoot is the legendary hairy creature of North American folklore.
lines.PIANO: In the film Big (an older film, but a famous scene), Tom Hanks dances out a tune on a giant floor piano.

hints.explanation: A tuning fork rings at a reference pitch, and guitars need regular tuning.

lines.FORK: A tuning fork is a two-pronged metal fork that hums at a set pitch.
lines.GUITAR: Guitarists tune their strings before playing.

hints.explanation: A trident is a three-pronged spear shaped like a giant fork, and Trident is a chewing gum brand.

lines.FORK: A trident looks like a giant three-pronged fork.
lines.GUM: Trident is a well-known brand of sugar-free gum.

hints.explanation: Dr. Seuss wrote the tongue-twister book Fox in Socks.

lines.FOX: A fox stars in Dr. Seuss's Fox in Socks.
lines.SOCK: The fox in Fox in Socks wears socks.

hints.explanation: The Louvre, the famous art museum in Paris, France, is entered through a giant glass pyramid.

lines.FRANCE: The Louvre is a famous art museum in Paris, France, home of the Mona Lisa.
lines.PYRAMID: A large glass pyramid, added in 1989, serves as the Louvre's main entrance.

hints.explanation: The storming of the Bastille in 1789 is remembered every July 14 in France as Bastille Day.

lines.FRANCE: France celebrates Bastille Day, its national holiday, on July 14.
lines.STORM: Revolutionaries stormed the Bastille fortress in Paris on July 14, 1789.

hints.explanation: A fair-weather friend sticks around only in good times, and fair weather is clear and pleasant.

lines.FRIEND: A fair-weather friend disappears when times get tough.
lines.WEATHER: Fair weather means clear, pleasant conditions.

hints.explanation: In Marvel's Thor films, Loki learns he was born a Frost Giant; in Norse myth he is the son of a giant.

lines.FROST: In the 2011 film Thor, Loki discovers he is a Frost Giant by birth.
lines.GIANT: In Norse myth, Loki is the son of a giant.

hints.explanation: Olive Garden is a chain of Italian-American restaurants, and olives are a staple of Italian cooking.

lines.GARDEN: Olive Garden is a U.S. chain of Italian-American restaurants.
lines.OLIVE: Olives and olive oil are staples of Italian cooking.

hints.explanation: The Hanging Gardens of Babylon and the Great Pyramid of Giza both appear on the list of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

lines.GARDEN: The Hanging Gardens of Babylon are traditionally listed among the Seven Wonders, though historians debate whether they existed.
lines.PYRAMID: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the only one of the Seven Wonders still standing.

hints.explanation: A carol is a Christmas song, and in A Christmas Carol three ghosts visit Scrooge.

lines.GHOST: In Dickens's A Christmas Carol, Scrooge is visited by ghosts, starting with Jacob Marley.
lines.SONG: A carol is a festive song, especially one sung at Christmas.

hints.explanation: In Gulliver's Travels, Gulliver is a giant among the tiny Lilliputians and small among the giants of Brobdingnag.

lines.GIANT: In Brobdingnag, Gulliver is tiny beside a land of giants.
lines.SMALL: In Lilliput, Gulliver towers over people only about six inches tall.

hints.explanation: Two idioms meet: never look a gift horse in the mouth, and hear news straight from the horse's mouth.

lines.GIFT: Don't look a gift horse in the mouth means don't pick faults in a present.
lines.MOUTH: Straight from the horse's mouth means from the most direct source, and the gift-horse idiom involves checking a horse's mouth too.

hints.explanation: Santa brings gifts at Christmas, and in a Secret Santa swap people give gifts anonymously.

lines.GIFT: Santa Claus is said to bring gifts to children at Christmas.
lines.SECRET: In a Secret Santa exchange, each person secretly buys a gift for someone else.

hints.explanation: A white elephant gift swap is a party exchange of funny or unwanted gifts.

lines.GIFT: In a white elephant exchange, guests bring wrapped gifts and can steal each other's picks.
lines.WHITE: A white elephant is a burdensome possession, the idea behind the white elephant party game.

hints.explanation: Pan, the Greek god of the wild, has the legs and horns of a goat and plays the pan pipes named for him.

lines.GOAT: The Greek god Pan is pictured with a goat's legs and horns.
lines.PIPE: Pan pipes, a set of tubes of different lengths, are named after the god Pan.

hints.explanation: Mercury is the Roman messenger god and the liquid metal in old-style thermometers.

lines.GOD: Mercury is the Roman messenger god.
lines.THERMOMETER: Older thermometers use liquid mercury that rises with heat.

hints.explanation: The bench press is a classic gym lift, and parks have benches to sit on.

lines.GYM: The bench press is a staple weightlifting exercise at the gym.
lines.PARK: A park bench is a classic place to sit outdoors.

hints.explanation: Rapunzel lets down her long hair from the tower so it can be climbed like a rope.

lines.HAIR: Rapunzel is famous for her extremely long hair.
lines.ROPE: In the fairy tale, Rapunzel's hair serves as a rope for climbing up the tower.

hints.explanation: Pumpkin carving is a Halloween tradition, and carving the turkey is a Thanksgiving tradition.

lines.HALLOWEEN: Carving jack-o'-lanterns from pumpkins is a Halloween tradition.
lines.THANKSGIVING: Carving the roast turkey is a classic Thanksgiving dinner moment.

hints.explanation: A hammer drives a nail, and to hit the nail on the head means to get something exactly right.

lines.HAMMER: A hammer is the classic tool for driving nails.
lines.HEAD: To hit the nail on the head is to describe something exactly right.

hints.explanation: "It's the Hard Knock Life" is a famous song from the musical Annie.

lines.HARD: The orphans in Annie sing that theirs is a "hard knock" life.
lines.LIFE: "It's the Hard Knock Life" is Annie's song about orphan life.

hints.explanation: Heavy metal is a loud, guitar-driven style of rock music.

lines.HEAVY: Heavy metal is a music genre known for loud, distorted guitars.
lines.ROCK: Heavy metal grew out of hard rock in the late 1960s and 1970s.

hints.explanation: In music, a hook is the catchy part of a song that sticks in your head.

lines.HOOK: A song's hook is its catchy riff or line, just as a fishing hook catches fish.
lines.SONG: A catchy song is one you can't stop humming.

hints.explanation: A shofar is a ram's horn blown like a trumpet on Jewish holidays such as Rosh Hashanah.

lines.HORN: A shofar is a musical instrument made from an animal horn.
lines.RAM: Shofars are traditionally made from a ram's horn.

hints.explanation: Cricket is both a chirping insect and a bat-and-ball sport popular in England and India.

lines.INSECT: A cricket is an insect known for its chirping.
lines.SPORT: Cricket is a bat-and-ball sport played widely in England, India and Australia.

hints.explanation: The harp is a stringed instrument, and the harp seal is a North Atlantic seal.

lines.INSTRUMENT: The harp is a large stringed instrument plucked by hand.
lines.SEAL: Harp seals are known for their fluffy white pups.

hints.explanation: Jack Frost is the folklore figure who brings frost and icy cold in winter.

lines.JACK: Jack Frost personifies frost in English folklore.
lines.WINTER: Jack Frost gets the credit for frosty winter mornings and icy windowpanes.

hints.explanation: Royal jelly is the bee food that larvae destined to become queens are fed in abundance.

lines.JELLY: Royal jelly is a secretion that worker bees feed to developing queen bees.
lines.QUEEN: A queen is royalty, and in a hive the queen bee is raised on royal jelly.

hints.explanation: The canopy is the jungle's high roof of treetops, and an umbrella's fabric top is also called its canopy.

lines.JUNGLE: The canopy is the dense upper layer of treetops in a jungle or rainforest.
lines.UMBRELLA: The fabric cover stretched over an umbrella's ribs is called its canopy.

hints.explanation: King Kong is found on the remote Skull Island.

lines.KING: King Kong is the giant ape of the classic film.
lines.SKULL: In King Kong, the giant ape lives on Skull Island (also the setting of the 2017 film Kong: Skull Island).

hints.explanation: The kiwi is New Zealand's national bird, and New Zealanders are nicknamed Kiwis.

lines.KIWI: The kiwi bird is a national symbol of New Zealand.
lines.NEW: New Zealand is the island country southeast of Australia.

hints.explanation: In legend, King Arthur's knights gathered at the Round Table.

lines.KNIGHT: King Arthur led the Knights of the Round Table.
lines.TABLE: In Arthurian legend, the Round Table seats Arthur's knights as equals.

hints.explanation: A four-leaf clover is a classic symbol of luck.

lines.LEAF: A lucky clover has four leaves instead of the usual three.
lines.LUCK: Finding a four-leaf clover is said to bring good luck.

hints.explanation: Zest is a brand of bar soap, and lemon zest is the grated outer peel of a lemon.

lines.LEMON: Lemon zest is the colorful outer peel, grated for flavor.
lines.SOAP: Zest is a long-running American brand of bar soap.

hints.explanation: You write a letter with a pen, and the saying goes that the pen is mightier than the sword.

lines.LETTER: A pen is the classic tool for writing a letter.
lines.SWORD: The pen is mightier than the sword means words can be stronger than force.

hints.explanation: In Super Mario games, a 1-Up gives the player an extra life.

lines.LIFE: 1-Up is video game slang for an extra life.
lines.MARIO: In Mario games, a green 1-Up Mushroom grants an extra life.

hints.explanation: In The Legend of Zelda video games, the hero Link quests for the Triforce, a relic made of golden triangles.

lines.LINK: Link, the hero of The Legend of Zelda games, often seeks pieces of the Triforce.
lines.TRIANGLE: The Triforce is drawn as three golden triangles forming one larger triangle.

hints.explanation: A litter box holds cat litter, and a sandbox holds play sand.

lines.LITTER: Indoor cats use a litter box.
lines.SAND: Kids play in a sandbox filled with sand.

hints.explanation: The Magic 8 Ball fortune toy is styled after the black 8-ball from pool.

lines.MAGIC: The Magic 8 Ball is a toy that answers yes-or-no questions.
lines.POOL: In pool, the black ball numbered 8 is called the 8-ball.

hints.explanation: Sets add up to a match in tennis ("game, set, match"), and you set the table before a meal.

lines.MATCH: In tennis, winning sets wins the match, as in "game, set, match."
lines.TABLE: To set the table is to lay out plates and utensils.

hints.explanation: Mercury is both a silvery metal that is liquid at room temperature and the planet closest to the Sun.

lines.METAL: Mercury is a metal that is liquid at room temperature.
lines.PLANET: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.

hints.explanation: Treasure hunters sweep beaches and fields with metal detectors.

lines.METAL: A metal detector beeps when it senses metal underground.
lines.TREASURE: Hobbyists use metal detectors to hunt for buried treasure like coins and rings.

hints.explanation: An Oreo has a sweet creme filling in the middle.

lines.MIDDLE: The creme filling sits in the middle of an Oreo.
lines.OREO: Oreo cookies sandwich a sweet creme filling between two chocolate wafers.

hints.explanation: Sergeant is a military rank, and Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band is a classic Beatles album.

lines.MILITARY: Sergeant is a rank for noncommissioned officers in the military.
lines.PEPPER: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band is a 1967 Beatles album.

hints.explanation: Fortune-telling psychics claim to read minds and also offer to read palms.

lines.MIND: Psychics claim to be able to read minds.
lines.PALM: Many psychics offer palm reading, telling fortunes from the lines on a hand.

hints.explanation: Models pose for photographers, and striking a pose means holding a dramatic stance.

lines.MODEL: Models pose for photographers and painters.
lines.STRIKE: To strike a pose is to hold a dramatic stance, as Madonna urges in Vogue.

hints.explanation: People say cheese to smile for a picture, and cartoon mice famously love cheese.

lines.MOUSE: In cartoons and stories, mice love cheese.
lines.PICTURE: Photographers say Say cheese! to get smiles for a picture.

hints.explanation: When the cat's away, the mice will play, says the old proverb.

lines.MOUSE: Cats chase mice, and in the proverb the mice play while the cat is gone.
lines.PLAY: When the cat's away, the mice will play means people misbehave when the boss is gone.

hints.explanation: Mummies and zombies are both undead monsters of horror stories.

lines.MUMMY: In horror films, mummies rise from their tombs as undead monsters.
lines.ZOMBIE: Zombies are reanimated corpses, classic undead creatures of horror.

hints.explanation: Netflix often drops whole seasons at once, and watching episode after episode of a show is called bingeing.

lines.NETFLIX: Netflix often releases full seasons at once, which invites binge-watching.
lines.SHOW: To binge a show is to watch many episodes in one sitting.

hints.explanation: New Jersey is a U.S. state, and a jersey is the shirt worn in team sports.

lines.NEW: New Jersey is a state on the U.S. East Coast.
lines.SPORT: Athletes in many team sports wear numbered jerseys.

hints.explanation: In Game of Thrones, House Stark rules the North and its family words are "Winter is coming."

lines.NORTH: House Stark rules the North in Game of Thrones.
lines.WINTER: "Winter is coming" is the Stark family motto (a familiar line even beyond the show's fans).

hints.explanation: PowerPoint is the Microsoft Office app for building presentations out of slides.

lines.OFFICE: PowerPoint is part of the Microsoft Office suite.
lines.SLIDE: A PowerPoint presentation is made of slides.

hints.explanation: Dove is a soap brand, and a dove carrying an olive branch is a classic symbol of peace.

lines.OLIVE: In the Noah's Ark story a dove returns with an olive leaf, and a dove with an olive branch became a peace symbol.
lines.SOAP: Dove is a well-known brand of soap and beauty bars.

hints.explanation: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa, and Leonardo is a shell-wearing Ninja Turtle.

lines.PAINTING: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa.
lines.SHELL: Leonardo of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles has a turtle shell.

hints.explanation: In Monopoly, a card can send you to Jail with the order "Do not pass Go."

lines.PASS: "Do not pass Go, do not collect $200" is a famous Monopoly instruction.
lines.PRISON: Monopoly's board has a Jail corner where players get stuck.

hints.explanation: The dove is a symbol of peace, and doves and pigeons belong to the same bird family.

lines.PEACE: A white dove is a classic symbol of peace.
lines.PIGEON: Doves and pigeons are both members of the same bird family.

hints.explanation: A pilot is the first test episode of a TV show, and a season is a run of episodes.

lines.PILOT: In TV, a pilot is a show's first episode, made to sell the series.
lines.SEASON: A TV season is made up of a set of episodes.

hints.explanation: In the song, Frosty the Snowman has a corncob pipe and a button nose.

lines.PIPE: The song gives Frosty the Snowman a corncob pipe.
lines.SNOWMAN: Frosty the Snowman is a snowman who comes to life in the classic holiday song.

hints.explanation: Someone with a green thumb is good at growing plants.

lines.PLANT: Most plants are green, and a green thumb means a knack for growing them.
lines.THUMB: Having a green thumb means you're a skilled gardener.

hints.explanation: Earth's crust is broken into tectonic plates, and many volcanoes form where those plates meet or pull apart.

lines.PLATE: Earth's outer shell is divided into huge tectonic plates.
lines.VOLCANO: Many volcanoes, like those around the Pacific Ring of Fire, form along tectonic plate boundaries.

hints.explanation: U.S. police read suspects their Miranda rights, starting with the right to remain silent.

lines.POLICE: U.S. police give a Miranda warning before questioning a suspect in custody.
lines.RIGHT: Miranda rights include the right to remain silent and the right to a lawyer.

hints.explanation: In Star Wars, a Padawan is a Jedi pupil, and Yoda is the famous Jedi Master teacher.

lines.PUPIL: A Padawan is the Star Wars term for a Jedi apprentice, essentially a pupil.
lines.YODA: Yoda is a Jedi Master who trains Jedi, including Luke Skywalker (Star Wars fans will know Padawan best).

hints.explanation: Sushi is made with vinegared rice, often wrapped into a roll.

lines.RICE: Sushi is built on rice seasoned with vinegar.
lines.ROLL: A sushi roll wraps rice and fillings in seaweed, then slices it.

hints.explanation: Sonic the Hedgehog collects gold rings, and "sonic" means related to sound.

lines.RING: Sonic the Hedgehog races through levels collecting gold rings.
lines.SOUND: Sonic means relating to sound, as in a sonic boom.

hints.explanation: Stones are rocks, and the Rolling Stones are famous for their tongue-and-lips logo.

lines.ROCK: Stones and rocks are near synonyms, and the Rolling Stones are a rock band.
lines.TONGUE: The Rolling Stones' logo is a pair of red lips with a tongue sticking out.

hints.explanation: In tug of war, two teams tug on opposite ends of a rope.

lines.ROPE: Tug of war is played by two teams pulling a rope.
lines.WAR: Tug of war pits two sides against each other in a mock war of strength.

hints.explanation: A dune is a hill of sand, and in Dune the desert planet Arrakis is the only source of the precious spice.

lines.SAND: A dune is a hill of sand built up by the wind.
lines.SPICE: In Dune, the spice melange is mined from the sands of the desert planet Arrakis.

hints.explanation: Show and tell is a school activity where kids bring in an item to show the class and tell about it.

lines.SCHOOL: Show and tell is a classic activity in elementary school classrooms.
lines.SHOW: In show and tell, a child shows something special and tells the class about it.

hints.explanation: Scuba diving goes under the sea, and skydiving drops from the sky.

lines.SCUBA DIVER: A scuba diver goes scuba diving with an air tank.
lines.SKY: Skydiving is jumping from a plane and free-falling through the sky.

hints.explanation: A "seal of approval" and a "stamp of approval" both mean an official thumbs-up.

lines.SEAL: A seal of approval marks something as officially endorsed.
lines.STAMP: A stamp of approval means formal endorsement.

hints.explanation: A skeleton in the closet is a shameful secret someone keeps hidden.

lines.SECRET: A skeleton in the closet is a secret someone would rather nobody found.
lines.SKELETON: The idiom pictures a skeleton hidden away in a closet.

hints.explanation: Hermes, the messenger god of Greek myth, is shown wearing winged sandals.

lines.SHOE: His winged sandals let Hermes speed between the gods and mortals.
lines.WING: Hermes is often pictured with little wings on his sandals and helmet.

hints.explanation: Missouri's nickname is the Show-Me State.

lines.SHOW: Missouri is nicknamed the Show-Me State, a nod to its no-nonsense skepticism.
lines.STATE: Missouri is a U.S. state in the Midwest.

hints.explanation: Sea sponges are animals whose bodies are full of pores, and human skin is dotted with pores too.

lines.SKIN: Skin has pores that release sweat and oil.
lines.SPONGE: Sea sponges belong to the phylum Porifera, meaning pore-bearing, and water flows in through their many pores.

hints.explanation: A mole is a spot on the skin and also a spy planted inside an organization.

lines.SKIN: A mole is a small dark spot on the skin.
lines.SPY: A mole is a spy who works secretly inside an organization.

hints.explanation: The Flash is a superfast superhero, while Flash in Zootopia is a famously slow sloth.

lines.SLOW: In Zootopia, Flash the sloth works painfully slowly at the DMV.
lines.SUPERHERO: The Flash is DC's super-speed superhero.

hints.explanation: Shakespeare wrote that a rose by any other name would smell as sweet.

lines.SMELL: In Romeo and Juliet, a rose would smell as sweet under any name.
lines.SWEET: Juliet says the rose would be just as sweet by another name.

hints.explanation: A snowman is often given a carrot nose, and the carrot is a classic root vegetable.

lines.SNOWMAN: A carrot is the traditional nose for a snowman.
lines.VEGETABLE: The carrot is a common root vegetable.

hints.explanation: Victoria Beckham was Posh Spice of the Spice Girls, and her husband David Beckham is a soccer star.

lines.SOCCER: David Beckham is a famous English soccer player.
lines.SPICE: Victoria Beckham was known as Posh Spice in the Spice Girls.

hints.explanation: Charmin toilet paper is famously advertised as soft.

lines.SOFT: Charmin sells lines such as Charmin Ultra Soft.
lines.TOILET: Charmin is a well-known brand of toilet paper.

hints.explanation: An old saying calls the eyes the window to the soul.

lines.SOUL: The eyes are said to reveal the soul.
lines.WINDOW: The saying pictures the eye as a window looking inward.

hints.explanation: James Bond is the famous fictional spy, and bonds are investments often paired with stocks.

lines.SPY: James Bond, 007, is fiction's most famous spy.
lines.STOCKS: Investors often balance stocks with bonds.

hints.explanation: A tempest is a violent storm, and a tempest in a teapot is a big fuss over something small.

lines.STORM: A tempest is a violent, windy storm.
lines.TEA: A tempest in a teapot means an uproar over a trivial matter.

hints.explanation: A heat wave is a stretch of extreme heat, most common in summer.

lines.SUMMER: Summer is the hottest season, the usual time for heat waves.
lines.WAVE: A heat wave is a run of unusually hot days.

hints.explanation: A tire swing is an old tire hung from a sturdy tree branch.

lines.SWING: A tire swing is a swing made from an old tire.
lines.TREE: Tire swings are usually hung by rope from a tree branch.

hints.explanation: Ticket to Ride is a Beatles song and a train-building board game, and you buy a ticket to ride a train.

lines.TICKET: Ticket to Ride is a Beatles hit and the name of a popular board game.
lines.TRAIN: In the Ticket to Ride board game, players build train routes across a map.

hints.explanation: In many sports a tied game goes to overtime, and overtime is extra hours at work.

lines.TIE: In many sports, a tie at the end of regulation goes to overtime.
lines.WORK: Overtime means working extra hours beyond a normal shift.

hints.explanation: In Disney's Tangled, Rapunzel is locked in a tower, and a famous line warns about the tangled web we weave when we deceive.

lines.TOWER: In Disney's Tangled, Rapunzel grows up locked away in a tower.
lines.WEB: Oh, what a tangled web we weave is a well-known line by Sir Walter Scott about deception.

hints.explanation: Mary Poppins arrives on the east wind and floats down holding her umbrella.

lines.UMBRELLA: Mary Poppins famously flies with her umbrella, which in the Disney film has a talking parrot-head handle.
lines.WIND: In the story, Mary Poppins arrives when the wind changes to the east.

hints.explanation: The White Stripes were a famous rock duo, and a zebra is covered in black and white stripes.

lines.WHITE: The White Stripes were a rock duo known for Seven Nation Army.
lines.ZEBRA: Zebras are covered in black and white stripes.
